element.name: Shard of Moonlight
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: This weapon is the flesh of a Great One carved away in pain and fashioned into a blade. The Shard of Moonlight is the reason the Shattered Moon exists and the Devouring Moon is no more. He who wields the blade is overwhelmed by hope, however misguided it might be…
While attuned to this weapon, you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: You are proficient with Greatswords and Longswords.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
You have Advantage on Wisdom saving throws, except those made to resist Madness.
You can use this weapon as a Spellcasting Focus.

description.p: Sentience. The Shard of Moonlight is a sentient weapon, with the same personality as the Great One whose flesh it was carved from. The weapon sporadically communicates telepathically with its wielder through images and sounds, though it doesn’t speak.

Trick Weapon. As a Bonus Action, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the shard is a metallic Longsword that absorbs light. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a Greatsword that pulses with lunar energy. In both states, this weapon has the Light property.

Untransformed. The Longsword deals an extra 1d6 Radiant damage on a hit, and it seems to guide your strikes. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with this weapon, you can immediately make a second attack (no action required). It has the Void Absorption property.

Void Absorption. The void that fills the blade is capable of absorbing magic. While holding the shard, you can take a Reaction to absorb a spell that is targeting you, including spells with an area of effect. The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy—not the spell itself—is stored in the shard in the form of charges. The number of charges gained is equivalent to the level of the spell when it was cast (1 charge for cantrips). The shard can absorb and store up to 10 charges. If the shard doesn’t have enough empty charges for a spell, it fails to absorb it. The shard regains all charges each time the moon changes.

Transformed. While under direct moonlight, you can take a Bonus Action to transform the shard. The transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you end it early as a Bonus Action, or when the shard loses all charges. The Greatsword deals an extra 2d6 Radiant damage on a hit. Each time you make an attack with the Greatsword, you can expend charges to create one of the following effects.

ul.li: Revealing Glow. As part of making an attack, you can expend 1 charge to empower the blade. On a hit, it deals an extra 1d12 Radiant damage, and until the start of your next turn, the target sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius. While affected by the light, the target can’t have the Invisible condition, and attack rolls against it have Advantage.

Transient Moonlight. As part of making an attack, you can expend 2 charges to release a wave of moonlight where the blade slashes, creating a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long Line of moonlight originating from you. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 2d12 Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Lunar Explosion. Instead of making an attack, you can expend 3 charges to raise the blade upward and release a burst of moonlight energy. Each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 3d12 Radiant damage and has the Prone condition. When a creature within 5 feet of you gains the Prone condition from this effect, you can take a Reaction to make a melee attack against the creature with this weapon. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

element.name: Sword of the Radiant Watcher
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: The Sword of the Radiant Watcher is an ancient weapon, meant to contain two entities bound into eternal hatred. One was a hunter and one was a beast, though no one knows which aspect of the blade they were bound to.

Sentience. This sentient weapon has two distinct personalities. The Angelic personality (alignment: Lawful Good) is protective and nurturing and linked to the Light Form of the weapon, while the Hateful personality (alignment: Chaotic Evil) is cunning and ruthless and linked to the Shadow Form of the weapon. The weapon has an Intelligence of 14, a Wisdom of 12, and a Charisma of 17. It has hearing and Darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. The dominant personality may attempt to influence the wielder's actions, particularly when it comes to matters of morality or strategy. However, the sword cannot force its wielder to act against their will. The sword communicates telepathically with its wielder and knows Common and Deep Speech.

Trick Weapon. As a Bonus Action, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon by letting hatred or hope overwhelm you. In both states, the weapon is a Longsword. When the weapon's form changes, so too does its dominant personality. The two personalities within the Sword of the Radiant Watcher are in a constant struggle for dominance. When the wielder attempts to switch the weapon’s forms, they must exert their force of will to do so, making a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. On a success, the sword changes form, and on a failure, it stubbornly refuses to do so until the start of your next turn, at which point you can attempt to switch the weapon’s forms again.
Untransformed: Light Form. The Angelic personality is dominant, and the Longsword deals an extra 1d8 Radiant damage on a hit.

ul.li: Curse of Light. When you hit a creature with this sword, you can bind the target to your light (no action required). For the next minute, you are under the effect of the Sanctuary spell (save DC 16), but only the bound target must make the saving throw. This effect ends as normal if you take an action that would break it but returns at the start of your next turn.

Retribution of Light. When a target is under the effect of the Curse of Light, you can take a Bonus Action to bolster up to four creatures of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet of yourself. For the duration of the curse, each chosen creature has Advantage on the first attack roll it makes against the target each turn, and if the attack hits, it deals extra damage equal to the creature’s Proficiency Bonus of one damage type that the attack dealt of the creature’s choice. This property of the weapon can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dawn.

description.p: Transformed: Shadow Form. The Hateful personality is dominant, and the Longsword deals an extra 1d8 Necrotic damage on a hit.

ul.li: Shadow Chain. When you hit a creature with this sword, you can tether the target to you with a chain of shadowy energy (no action required). While tethered, the creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet, and neither you nor the creature can willingly move or teleport more than 30 feet away from each other. The tether lasts for 1 minute or until you use this property on another creature, you start your turn more than 30 feet away from the target, or you end the tether as a Bonus Action.

Shadow Consumption. While tethered to a creature with your Shadow Chain, once on each of your turns when you hit the target with this weapon, you can inflict an extra 3d6 Necrotic damage and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. This property of the weapon can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dawn.

description.p: Aborrhant Existence. The sentient entities within the sword are antithetical to each other, and no creature can withstand their presence at once, which is why the blade was sealed in such a way. If both forms of the sword damage the same creature in a single turn, that creature must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or gain a Short-Term Madness. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

In addition, if you deal Necrotic damage with the Shadow Form of the sword to the creature affected by Curse of Light, or conversely, if you deal Radiant damage with the Light Form of the sword to the creature affected by Shadow Chain, the effect ends and detonates. The target and each other creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the target makes a DC 16 Constitution saving throw, taking 2d6 Radiant damage and 2d6 Necrotic damage on a failed save as the antithetical energies resonate and self-destruct. You have Advantage on this saving throw.

element.name: Thirsting Épée Sanguine
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: While attuned to this weapon, you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 2d8 Necrotic damage on a hit.
You have Immunity to Poison damage, Necrotic damage, and the Poisoned condition.
You know the exact location of any creature with blood within 30 feet of yourself, even if it has the Invisible condition or is on the Ethereal Plane.

description.p: The weapon has the Blooddrinker and Lifestealing properties.

Blooddrinker. Each time you deal damage with this weapon to a creature that possesses blood, the Thirsting Épée Sanguine gains 1 charge. The épée can hold up to 6 charges. Each charge lasts for 1 minute or until it is expended.

Lifestealing. In dire situations, the épée grants you the power to take the life of others. If you are reduced to one-quarter of your Hit Points or fewer, you can immediately use this property (no action required). Until the end of your next turn, whenever you deal damage using this weapon, you regain Hit Points equal to the damage dealt. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Trick Weapon. As a Bonus Action while this weapon has 1 or more charges, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the blade is a vile Longsword glowing with echoes of blood. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a Greatsword with an even more nefarious aspect.
Untransformed. You gain a 1d12 bonus to attack rolls you make with this Longsword against creatures that are at their Hit Point maximum. In addition, the weapon has the Blood Shield property.
Blood Shield. The épée forms a barrier of blood around you with the blood it has absorbed. You gain a +1 bonus to AC for each 2 charges within the épée.

Transformed. You gain a 1d6 bonus to attack rolls you make with this Greatsword against creatures that are below their Hit Point maximum. In this form, the Thirsting Épée Sanguine consumes 1 charge at the end of each of your turns unless you've expended 1 or more charges that turn. It reverts back to its Untransformed state if it loses all charges.
When you hit a creature with an attack using the Greatsword, you can expend 1 or more charges to unleash the blood accumulated in the blade:

ul.li: 1 Charge. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage you dealt.
2 Charges. You deal an extra 2d8 Necrotic damage and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage you dealt.

3 Charges. The target becomes bound in blood and must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 4d6 Necrotic damage and has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

4 Charges. Blood covers the creature’s face and chokes it. The target must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 4d10 Necrotic damage and has the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

element.name: Unbound Épée Solaire
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: The method to create the Unbound Épée Solaire is a tightlipped secret, involving harnessing the power of the sun, a method that only devout followers of the Radiant One can grasp. As time went on, the sun faded from the skies of Luyarnha, replaced by a never ending night, and so, the creation of this weapon became impossible. This weapon was bathed in the blood of the sun, unleashing its potential.
While attuned to this weapon, you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: You are proficient with Greatswords and Shortswords.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1d8 Radiant damage on a hit. When you hit an Aberration or Undead with it, the extra Radiant damage increases to 2d8.
You have Advantage on saving throws against Madness.

description.p: The weapon has the Brilliant Light and Deflective Light properties.

Brilliant Light. The weapon’s blade emits Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. The light is sunlight. You can summon or extinguish the light at will (no action required). Each creature of your choice in the light has Resistance to Radiant damage.

Deflective Light. When you are attacked by a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself while holding this weapon, you can take a Reaction to cause a burst of sunlight to flare before the attacker, imposing Disadvantage on the attack roll and transforming this weapon. An attacker is immune to this effect if it is immune to the Blinded condition.

Trick Weapon. As a Bonus Action, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the weapon is a metallic Greatsword glowing with light. In its Transformed state, the weapon is two Shortswords emitting the same glow.
Untransformed. While wielding this Greatsword, your senses are pushed to their limit. You gain a +1 bonus to AC and all saving throws. In addition, the weapon has the Light of Judgment property.

Light of Judgment. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash judgment upon the heretics. The Brilliant Light of this weapon is summoned for the next minute or until you have the Unconscious condition or transform the weapon. You and all enemies within the Bright Light immediately take 2d8 Radiant damage. In addition, for the duration, you deal an extra 2d8 Radiant damage whenever you damage a creature with this weapon.

Transformed. When you make the extra attack of the Light property with these Shortswords, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the extra attack. In addition, this weapon gains the Sunscorch property.

Sunscorch. Whenever you hit a creature two times in a turn with these Shortswords, the accumulated solar energy detonates. The target and each other creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the target makes a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 3d10 Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
